turns.customer: Dyson V6 Pulising
turns.reply:
A Dyson V6 that pulses on and off is almost always short of airflow. That usually means a blocked or damp filter, or a blockage somewhere. The motor cuts in and out to protect itself.

Start with the filters:
1. Take the battery off the charger or unplug it. Empty the bin.
2. Take the filters out and wash them in cold water until the water runs clear. Don't use soap.
3. Let them dry completely for at least 24 hours before you put them back. Even a slightly damp filter can cause pulsing.

Were the filters clogged or damp? Is either one damaged? Or were they already clean and dry? Once they're refitted, does it still pulse?
media: Poor suction — what to check first

turns.customer: filter is blocked
turns.reply:
A blocked filter is very likely why your V6 is pulsing. Not enough air gets through, so the motor keeps cutting out to protect itself.

To get it running properly again:
1. Wash the filter in cold water and keep going until the water runs clear. It may need several rinses.
2. Leave it to dry for a full 24 hours. A damp filter will still make it pulse.
3. Refit it, put the battery back on, and run it on normal mode.

If the filter still looks clogged or discoloured after washing, it's worn out and needs replacing. If so, I can find you the right one.

Once it's dry and back in, does it run smoothly or is it still pulsing?

turns.customer: the filter is actually damaged
turns.reply:
A damaged filter can't be fixed by washing, so it needs replacing. Once air can't flow through it properly, the motor keeps cutting out to protect itself, and that's the pulsing you're seeing.

Your V6 has two filters, and I've listed both below:
1. The pre-motor filter sits in the top of the cyclone, above the bin. Order the Pre Filter Assembly for this one.
2. The post-motor HEPA filter is the round cap at the back of the motor. Order the Hepa Post Motor Filter (non-genuine) for this one.

Fit the new filter with the battery off. If the other filter is still good, make sure it's clean and completely dry before it goes back in.

Which filter is damaged? Once the new one is in, does it run without pulsing?
parts: Hepa Post Motor Filter Non Genuine

turns.customer: vax upright brush thingy stopped spinnin, sucks ok thru the hose but nt pickin up off carpet. smelt like burnin rubber b4 it stopped
turns.reply:
A burning rubber smell just before the brush stopped almost always means the drive belt slipped and then snapped or stretched. That usually happens because hair or thread jammed the brushbar. Suction through the hose is fine, so the motor itself sounds OK.

Here's the one check to do now:
1. Switch off and unplug the vacuum, then lay it face down.
2. Take off the brushbar cover plate (it's held by clips or a few screws) and lift out the brushbar.
3. Cut away any wrapped hair, and check whether the belt is snapped, loose or glazed.

If the belt is damaged it needs replacing. Can you send the model number? It's usually on a label on the back or underneath. What did you find?

turns.customer: turned it over, loads of hair n a tassel round the ends, cut it off and it spins free now. took the cover off and the belt is snapped in 2 bits. its a U85-AS-Be
turns.reply:
Good work. That's your fault found. The tassel and hair jammed the brushbar, the belt slipped and burnt (that was the rubber smell), and then it snapped. The belt needs replacing. For your U85-AS-Be we have a compatible (non-genuine) toothed belt, the 3M-207-6, for £7.00.

When it arrives:
1. With the vacuum still unplugged, loop the new belt round the motor pulley, then over the brushbar.
2. Seat the brushbar back in its end slots and check it turns freely by hand.
3. Refit the cover plate, then tilt the head and switch on to watch the bar.

Is the brushbar spinning once the new belt's in?

turns.customer: indesit oven stoped heating, fan goes round n light on but its stone cold after 20 mins. grill werks fine tho. any ideas b4 i call some1 out
turns.reply:
The fan turning shows the fan motor is fine, and the grill working shows the oven is getting power. The most likely cause is the fan-oven element (the ring behind the fan cover) failing. A burnt connector or a worn contact in the function knob can do the same thing, so it isn't certain yet.

First, rule out the setting, because defrost runs the fan with no heat:
1. Turn the function knob to the fan symbol with a ring around it (not just a plain fan, and not light-only or eco).
2. Turn the temperature knob to 180°C and check the temperature light comes on.
3. Leave it for 15 minutes.

Does it heat up now? Does the temperature light come on and then go off?

turns.customer: clock is set, nothing flashing. its an IFW 6330 IX. switched off at the cooker switch and took the back panel off, theres a blister and a split in the round element near the bottom with a black mark
turns.reply:
That's what's wrong. A split, blistered element with a scorch mark has burnt out, so the fan element needs replacing. The 1800W fan element for your IFW 6330 IX is £30.00. It's usually a straightforward swap. Keep the oven switched off at the cooker switch, then:
1. Take out the fan cover inside the oven and undo the element's screws.
2. From the back, take a photo of which wire goes on which terminal, then pull the connectors off.
3. Look closely at the connectors and wire ends. If any are burnt, brittle or discoloured, they need replacing too, or the new element can fail.

Are the connectors clean, or is there any burning on them?

turns.customer: Hi, my Bosch WAN28281GB has stopped half way through a wash and is showing E18. Water still in the drum. What does that mean?
turns.reply:
I can't confirm what E18 means on your model right now, so I'll go from what you're seeing. If it stops mid-wash with water left in the drum, the usual cause is that it can't drain, and most often that's a blocked pump filter (coins, hair grips, fluff).
1. Switch off and unplug the machine. If the wash was hot, let the water cool first.
2. Open the small flap at the bottom front. Put towels and a shallow tray down, then use the little drain hose (if yours has one) to let the water out slowly.
3. Unscrew the filter anticlockwise, clean it out, check the opening behind it for anything stuck, then screw it back in firmly.
Did you find anything in there, and does it drain now?

turns.customer: cleaned the filter, there was a sock and a hair grip in it. ran a drain and spin and it drains fast now, E18 gone
turns.reply:
Great work. The sock and hair grip were blocking the pump filter, so the machine couldn't drain and stopped mid-wash. Now that it drains quickly and E18 has cleared, that blockage looks like the whole problem. Nothing needs replacing.
One last check:
1. Make sure the filter cap is screwed in fully and straight.
2. Run a normal wash and check the floor by the bottom flap during the drain and spin.
3. To stop it happening again, wash socks and small items in a mesh bag and check pockets for hair grips and coins before washing.
Did the wash finish properly, and is the floor dry?

turns.customer: Bosch integrated dishwasher showing E:15 and the pump keeps running. Model SMV4HTX31E. I've turned it off and on, still there
turns.reply:
I can't confirm what E:15 means on your model right now, so I'll go by what you're seeing. If the drain pump keeps running and the machine won't start a wash, that usually means water has got into the base tray. The float has picked it up and the machine is pumping out to protect itself. The real fault is a leak somewhere, not the pump.

Please check the base:
1. Switch it off at the wall socket or isolator and turn off the water tap.
2. Unclip or unscrew the kickboard (the panel below the door).
3. Shine a torch underneath and look for water in the base tray or on the floor.

Is it wet under there or dry? Please don't run it again until we know.

turns.customer: LG F4V5VYP0W says OE and the clothes are sat in water. I'm not opening the little door at the bottom because last time I did that it flooded the whole kitchen. What else can I do?
turns.reply:
I can't look up OE on your model right now, so I can't confirm what it means. Clothes left sitting in water mean the machine isn't draining, though. The usual causes are a blocked pump filter or a blocked or kinked drain hose. Let's check the hose end first, since that needs no flap opening:
1. Switch off and unplug the machine.
2. Ease it out and check the grey drain hose isn't kinked or squashed behind it.
3. Where the hose joins the sink waste or standpipe, unclip it and clear any blockage. A new sink trap with its blanking disc still in place is a common one.

Next time the filter does need doing, towels and a baking tray help. What did you find?

turns.customer: hose was squashed behind the machine, pulled it out and straightened it. drained a bit slower than normal then OE again
turns.reply:
I still can't confirm what OE means on your model, but it drained slowly and then stopped again, so the pump filter is almost certainly partly blocked. You can drain it in a controlled way so the kitchen doesn't flood:
1. Switch off and unplug the machine. Lay towels down and put a baking tray or shallow dish in front of the flap.
2. Open the flap and look for a small rubber tube with a cap next to the filter. Pull it out, uncap it over the tray and let the water trickle out. Recap it each time the tray fills.
3. Only once that tube stops running, unscrew the filter slowly over towels and clear out any fluff, coins or grit.

Is there a drain tube there, and what did you find in the filter?

turns.customer: microwave not working, display shows the time and there's a little L symbol, buttons beep but it won't start
turns.reply:
That little L next to the time usually means the child lock (control lock) is on. When it's on, the buttons still beep but the microwave won't start, so it's very likely nothing is broken.

To turn it off:
1. Press and hold Stop/Cancel for about 3 to 5 seconds until it beeps and the L goes away. If that doesn't work, try holding Start for the same time. Some models use a key or lock button instead.
2. Put a cup of water inside and try a minute on full power.

Did the L go away, and does it start now? If not, tell me the make and model. You'll usually find them on a label inside the door frame or on the back.

turns.customer: Bosch WTN85201GB condenser dryer not drying properly anymore, clothes still damp after 2 hrs. any ideas
turns.reply:
On a condenser dryer like your Bosch WTN85201GB, damp clothes after 2 hours are most often caused by a blocked airflow path. Usually that's a fluffed-up condenser unit or fluff filter, and you can clear both yourself without any parts.

1. Switch the dryer off, unplug it and let it cool. Take the fluff filter out of the door opening and clear and rinse it.
2. Open the flap at the bottom front, unclip the condenser unit and slide it out. Rinse the fluff out of it under the tap until water runs through freely.
3. Let it drip-dry, refit it firmly, then run a normal drying programme with a normal-sized load.

Was the condenser clogged, and does it dry properly now?
media: Tumble dryer runs but doesn't heat — what to check

turns.customer: Just had a new induction hob fitted, Beko. When I put my saucepan on it just flashes a U and doesn't heat. Is it faulty? It's brand new!!
turns.reply:
I can't confirm what U means on your exact Beko model, but on induction hobs a flashing U or pan symbol usually means the zone can't detect a suitable pan. That's normal, and it's very often the saucepan rather than the hob. Induction only heats pans that are magnetic, have a flat base and are big enough for the zone.

With the hob switched off:
1. Hold a fridge magnet against the bottom of the saucepan. It has to stick firmly.
2. Check the base sits flat and roughly covers the ring marked on the zone.
3. If the magnet sticks, try the same pan on another zone.

It would only point to a fault if a magnetic pan of the right size still isn't detected on any zone. Did the magnet stick?

turns.customer: oven wont come on, display is flashing 0.00, we had a power cut last night
turns.reply:
That's almost certainly not a fault. A flashing 0.00 after a power cut usually means the clock has reset and put the oven into automatic (timed) mode, so it won't heat until you set it back to manual.

1. Press the manual button (often a hand or cooking-pot symbol). On many ovens you press two buttons together instead, often the + and - or the two middle buttons, until the flashing stops.
2. Set the correct time with the + and - buttons.
3. Choose a function and temperature and check it heats.

Please don't turn it off at the wall to reset it, because that puts it back into automatic mode.

Did that get it heating? If not, tell me the make and what buttons or symbols are on the clock.

turns.customer: my washin mashine wont turn on at all no lights nothin. its built in, kettle works in the other sockets
turns.reply:
With no lights at all, the most likely cause is that the machine isn't getting power. Built-in machines usually run through a separate switch on the wall, and that switch can be off or its fuse can have blown. Working sockets elsewhere don't rule this out.

1. Look on the wall above or near the worktop for a switch marked "washing machine" or one with a small fuse holder. Make sure it's switched on.
2. If it has a fuse holder, switch it off first. Then take out the fuse and swap in a known-good 13A fuse.
3. Switch it back on and try the machine.

Did you find a switch like that, and did the machine come on? If not, what make and model is it?

turns.customer: Hi, I've got a Dyson V15 Detect (SV22) about 4 months old. When I go from the kitchen tiles onto the lounge rug the motor suddenly gets much louder and the battery number drops faster, then it calms down again when I go back on the tiles. Also the screen goes up and down by itself. Is the motor on its way out?
turns.reply:
Good news: this sounds like normal behaviour, not a failing motor. In Auto mode the V15 Detect senses the floor and how much dust it's picking up. On a rug it turns the suction up, so it gets louder and uses battery faster. The number on the screen is the runtime left, and it goes up and down as the power changes.

To check:
1. Press the mode button on top until the screen shows Eco.
2. Go from the tiles onto the rug.
3. Listen. The sound and the runtime should stay roughly steady.

It would be a fault if you heard a screech, grinding or rough roar, or if it pulsed or cut out. Does it stay steady on Eco?

turns.customer: We bought a new heat pump tumble dryer last month and a normal cotton load takes over 3 hours. Our old vented one took about an hour. Is it faulty?
turns.reply:
That sounds normal rather than a fault. A heat pump dryer works like a fridge in reverse. It dries at a lower temperature, so it takes much longer than a vented dryer and clothes come out warm, not hot. Two to three hours for a full cotton load is typical. It would only be a fault if clothes were still damp at the end of a full programme, or if drying got slower over time.

To keep it as quick as it can be:
1. Clean the fluff filter in the door opening after every load.
2. Rinse the second filter behind the flap at the bottom front every few loads.
3. Spin clothes on the washer's fastest suitable speed and fill the drum no more than two-thirds.

Do the clothes come out properly dry at the end?

turns.customer: My dishwasher leaves plastic tubs and the inside of the door wet at the end of the eco programme. Glasses are fine. Is it broken?
turns.reply:
That sounds normal, not broken. Plastic holds very little heat, so water doesn't dry off it the way it does from glass and china. Eco programmes also dry gently, mostly by condensation, which is why the inside of the door is wet too. Your glasses coming out dry suggests the machine is heating properly.

The thing that helps most is rinse aid:
1. Check the rinse aid dispenser next to the detergent drawer and fill it up if it's low.
2. If it was already full, turn up the rinse aid dose in the settings.
3. When the programme finishes, open the door slightly and leave the dishes for 15 to 20 minutes.

It would be a fault if glass and china came out cold and wet too. Did the rinse aid need topping up?

turns.customer: Strong smell of gas in the kitchen and there was a whoosh when I lit the gas oven
turns.reply: If you can smell gas, treat it as an emergency: don't turn any switches on or off and no naked flames. Turn the gas off at the meter if you safely can, open doors and windows, and leave if the smell is strong. Call the National Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999.

turns.customer: There's a burning smell coming from my vented tumble dryer when it's on
turns.reply:
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer.

On a vented dryer, a burning smell is most often fluff (lint) that has built up around the heater because the airflow is blocked. That's a fire risk, so the first job is to find and clear the fluff.

With the dryer unplugged and cool:
1. Take out the fluff filter in the door opening. Clean it fully and look into the slot it sits in for any packed fluff.
2. Pull the dryer out and check the vent hose at the back. It should be short, with no kinks or squashed sections, and clear all the way to the outside vent.
3. Look for any scorch marks or melted plastic.

Was the filter or hose clogged with fluff, and did you see any scorching? Please don't run it again until we've talked it through.

turns.customer: My Shark cordless battery got really hot on charge last night and this morning it looks puffed up, the plastic case has split at the seam a bit. Can I still use it till a new one comes? It's the IZ201UK.
turns.reply:
A swollen, very hot or chemical-smelling battery can catch fire. Stop using and charging it now, unplug the charger, and if it is safe to move put it somewhere non-flammable away from anything that could burn. Don't puncture, squeeze or try to open the battery, and don't put it in the household bin — take it to a battery recycling point.

No, please don't use it or charge it again, not even until a new one comes.

Our parts shop doesn't list a battery for the IZ201UK. The next step:
1. Get a genuine replacement battery for the IZ201UK from Shark or a reputable stockist.
2. Don't put the swollen battery in household rubbish or recycling. Ask your local council or a battery recycling point how to dispose of a damaged lithium battery.

Is the vacuum still under Shark's warranty? If it is, they may replace the battery for free.

turns.customer: My Beko washing machine is leaking at the front and the water is spreading across the floor towards the socket
turns.reply:
Water near the plug or socket is dangerous. Please don't touch the plug, socket or machine if they or your hands are wet. If you can do it safely, switch off the circuit at the consumer unit (fuse box), keep away from the water, and don't use the machine again until a qualified electrician or appliance engineer has checked it.

Water at the front of a washing machine usually comes from the rubber door seal: either something is caught in its folds or the seal is torn. Less often it runs down from the detergent drawer above.

Once the machine is safe to approach (see the safety warning above), and without running it again:
1. Open the door and slowly peel back the folds of the rubber seal all the way round.
2. Look for anything trapped, like a coin, an underwire or fluff, and for any splits or perished patches, especially at the bottom.
3. Look at the front below the detergent drawer for drips or residue.

What did you find? Was the seal clear and intact, was something caught in it or was it torn?

turns.customer: My microwave runs but doesn't heat. I want to take the cover off and test the magnetron with my multimeter, how do I do that?
turns.reply:
I can't guide any testing or work inside a microwave — the high-voltage capacitor can hold a lethal charge even when it is unplugged, so the casing should only be opened by a qualified engineer.

If it starts and runs normally (light on, turntable turning, timer counting down) but stays cold, the most likely cause is a fault in the high-voltage heating circuit. That could be the magnetron or another high-voltage part. I can't walk you through opening the casing or testing it, because the parts inside are dangerous even when it's unplugged. Finding which part has failed is a job for a microwave engineer.

First, let's rule out a simple setting problem:
1. Make sure it's on full power, not defrost, grill or combi.
2. Heat a cup of water for one minute.
3. Check that the door latches firmly.

Is the water hot or still cold? And what's the make and model?

turns.customer: freezer stoped freezing alltogether, fridge warm too, compresser is running and the back is warm. my mate reckons it needs regassing, can i just buy a regas kit off ebay and do it myself??
turns.reply:
I can't help with re-gassing or opening the cooling circuit — it's sealed and pressurised (and often uses a flammable gas), so only a refrigeration engineer should work on it. Please don't pierce or cut any pipes.

Please don't do the regas yourself. It's a sealed-system job for a qualified refrigeration engineer. And it isn't certain yours needs gas. When the compressor runs but both sections go warm, it can be a refrigerant problem. But on a frost-free model it's often a thick block of ice choking the airflow, and you can check for that safely.

1. Open the freezer and look at the back wall inside, and in the drawers.
2. Look for heavy frost or a solid sheet of ice, rather than a light dusting.
3. Check the temperature setting is about -18°C and no holiday or eco mode is on.

Did you find heavy ice, and is it a frost-free model? If there's no ice and the settings are right, it'll need an engineer.

turns.customer: My combi boiler pressure keeps dropping, I have to top it up every few days
turns.reply:
Sorry, boilers and central heating aren't something we cover. We help with washing machines, washer-dryers, tumble dryers, dishwashers, fridges and freezers, ovens and cookers, hobs, microwaves and vacuum cleaners.

If your combi keeps losing pressure, that usually means water is escaping somewhere. It could be a small leak in the system, or a fault in the boiler such as the pressure relief valve or expansion vessel. Please book a Gas Safe registered engineer to find and fix it. Until then, it's fine to keep an eye out for drips under the boiler and around radiator valves.

If you have a problem with any of the appliances above, just tell me and I'll help.

turns.customer: freezer alarm keeps beeping, i think the door was left open a bit overnight. the display says -9
turns.reply:
This sounds like the freezer's temperature alarm doing its job. -9 is most likely the current freezer temperature, not an error code. With the door open overnight it has warmed up from the normal -18, and it will keep beeping until it gets cold again.

1. Check nothing is sticking out or blocking the door, then close it firmly and make sure the seal grips all the way round.
2. Press the alarm or alarm-off button to silence it. Most models have one.
3. Keep the door shut for 4 to 6 hours and let it cool back down.

If it doesn't get back near -18 by tomorrow, or the alarm keeps going with the door shut properly, that points to a fault. What does the display show after a few hours?
